assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly validated immuno-oncology target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical evidence. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1,700 ChEMBL IC50 entries are recorded, and 80 PDB structures including sub-angstrom resolution co-crystal structures confirm a well-defined binding interface. Druggability is high, though the dominant modality remains biologics; small-molecule inhibitors face challenges due to the relatively flat protein-protein interaction surface.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 interface remains challenging due to its flat, hydrophobic character — approved drugs are all biologics, and small-molecule clinical success is limited
Resistance mechanisms and predictive biomarkers for PD-L1 inhibition are still incompletely understood
Structural coverage of full-length transmembrane and intracellular domains is absent (structures focus on the extracellular IgV domain)
Combination therapy contexts and optimal patient stratification strategies are still under active investigation
Non-antibody modalities (e.g., peptides, macrocycles, small molecules) have sparse clinical validation despite ChEMBL entries
